newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-IGNORED HICK HELPS EMBARRASS AUSSIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-IGNORED HICK HELPS EMBARRASS AUSSIES.

text.p: Graeme Hick, ignored by England but still adored at Worcester, hit the day's top score as Australia were humbled by five wickets on Sunday.
On a day when he was overlooked for England's team to face Australia in the forthcoming one-day series, the Zimbabwe-born Hick made a crucial 35 as his side beat the tourists by five wickets.
The Australians were dismissed for just 121 and Worcestershire knocked off the runs with more than 11 overs to spare.
Their Western Australian captain, Tom Moody, said England's selectors had got it wrong by leaving Hick, a former test stalwart, out of the Texaco Trophy one-day squad.
"I'm surprised Graeme's not in the squad. To my mind he's too good a player in one-day cricket to leave him out," Moody said.
"I think he would have definitely been selected if he had made runs this season, but his lack of a few good early scores has made life difficult for him.
"But he's beginning to hit the ball as well as he can, and from his point of view he will be pressing now to regain his Test place."
Hick's knock steadied Worcestershire after two wickets in successive balls by the outstanding Mike Kasprowicz had left the home side 65 for three.

But by then Hick had already spanked Shane Warne through extra cover for four and, although the demon leg-spinner took two wickets in a thoughtful spell, the Aussies knew they had simply not made enough runs.
To cap it all for the unhappy Aussies, their team coach had to be winched out of a muddy car park by a recovery truck.
The Australians were certainly unsettled by a damp pitch and ideal conditions for the steady medium pace of David Leatherdale and Gavin Haynes.
Haynes led the way by bowling his 10 overs straight through and taking the first four Aussie wickets for 40 runs. Then Leatherdale, 29, produced the spell of his career to shock Mark Taylor's team.
He took five for 10 from five overs, his best analysis in any form of senior cricket.
"We did not bat well enough, and it is very disappointing," Taylor admitted.

"We did not tough it out in the middle order, and yesterday at Northampton we also did not get the sort of total we should have made. We talked about being more solid today, but it did not happen and we now have to do better at Durham on Tuesday."
To be fair to Australia, they rested perhaps their two strongest batsmen _ Mark Waugh and Michael Slater _ for the match.
